title: Create worker-config ConfigMap
description:
Create a ConfigMap in the `claude-workers` namespace with configuration settings for the queue scheduler.

Initial settings:
- `maxConcurrent: "2"` — maximum number of simultaneously running Claude sessions
- `rateLimitCooldownMinutes: "300"` — how long to wait before retrying after a rate limit hit (5 hours matches Claude's rolling window)

The scheduler Deployment will mount this ConfigMap and re-read it on each loop iteration so settings can be changed without restarting the scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: `kubectl apply -f agents/worker-config.yaml` creates the ConfigMap in claude-workers
ConfigMap has maxConcurrent and rateLimitCooldownMinutes keys
README documents how to change settings: `kubectl edit configmap worker-config -n claude-workers`

title: Implement queue-aware entrypoint wait loop
description:
Update `agents/base-image/entrypoint.sh` to wait for the scheduler to release the pod before launching Claude.

New flow at startup:
1. Configure git credentials (unchanged)
2. **NEW: Wait loop** — poll every 5 seconds until pod label `status` is `running`:
   ```bash
   echo "Waiting for queue release..."
   while true; do
     STATUS=$(kubectl get pod "$HOSTNAME" -n claude-workers \
       -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.status}' 2>/dev/null)
     [ "$STATUS" = "running" ] && break
     sleep 5
   done
   echo "Released by scheduler, starting work..."
   ```
3. Clone repo, checkout branch, start Claude (unchanged after this point)

Note: For Phase 1 compatibility, if the pod was created with `status=running` (manual launch without the scheduler), the wait loop exits immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Pod created with status=queued waits before cloning repo or starting Claude
Pod starts Claude immediately after label changes to status=running
Pod created with status=running (legacy/manual) starts Claude immediately
"Waiting for queue release" message appears in pod logs
Wait loop does not consume excessive CPU (5 second sleep between checks)

title: Build queue scheduler Deployment
description:
Create a Deployment in `claude-workers` namespace that runs a bash loop every 30 seconds to promote queued pods.

Scheduler logic (`agents/scheduler/entrypoint.sh`):
```
while true; do
  sleep 30
  MAX=$(kubectl get configmap worker-config ... maxConcurrent)
  RUNNING=$(kubectl get pods ... status=running | count)
  
  if RUNNING < MAX:
    OLDEST_QUEUED = oldest pod with status=queued
    if exists:
      kubectl label pod OLDEST_QUEUED status=running --overwrite
      echo "Released: OLDEST_QUEUED"
done
```

The Deployment:
- 1 replica
- Small resources: 100m CPU, 128Mi RAM
- Uses the `claude-worker` ServiceAccount (already has pod patch permissions)
- Uses a minimal image: `bitnami/kubectl:latest` or similar (needs kubectl + bash)
- Mounts worker-config ConfigMap

Create RBAC additions if needed: the ServiceAccount needs `list` and `get` on pods (in addition to `patch` from Phase 1).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler Deployment runs and stays healthy
Starting 3 tasks with maxConcurrent=1 results in 1 running and 2 queued
When a running task finishes (status=done), the next queued task starts within 30s
Scheduler logs show which pods it releases
Scheduler handles empty queue gracefully (no errors when nothing to promote)

title: Add Claude Code hooks for usage limit detection
description:
Implement detection of Claude API usage limit hits so pods can self-report their rate-limited status.

Approach: wrap the Claude invocation in the entrypoint with output parsing:

```bash
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions ... 2>&1 | tee /workspace/.claude-output.log
EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

# Check output for rate limit signals
if grep -qiE "rate.?limit|usage.?limit|too many requests|overloaded" \
    /workspace/.claude-output.log; then
  COOLDOWN=$(kubectl get configmap worker-config ... rateLimitCooldownMinutes)
  RETRY_AFTER=$(date -d "+${COOLDOWN} minutes" +%s)
  kubectl annotate pod "$HOSTNAME" ccw/retry-after="$RETRY_AFTER" --overwrite
  kubectl label pod "$HOSTNAME" status=rate-limited --overwrite
  echo "Rate limit hit. Will retry after $(date -d @$RETRY_AFTER)"
elif [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then
  kubectl label pod "$HOSTNAME" status=done --overwrite
else
  kubectl label pod "$HOSTNAME" status=error --overwrite
fi
```

Also create `agents/base-image/hooks/on-stop.sh` as a Claude Code Stop hook (configured in `~/.claude/settings.json`) as a secondary detection mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: When Claude output contains rate limit text, pod label changes to status=rate-limited
Pod annotation ccw/retry-after is set to a valid future Unix timestamp
Normal completion still sets status=done
Error exits still set status=error
Rate limit detection is case-insensitive and matches common variations

title: Implement rate limit recovery in scheduler
description:
Extend the scheduler loop to re-queue rate-limited pods when their cooldown expires.

Addition to scheduler loop:
```bash
# Check rate-limited pods
for POD in $(kubectl get pods -n claude-workers -l status=rate-limited ...):
  RETRY_AFTER=$(kubectl get pod $POD ... annotation ccw/retry-after)
  NOW=$(date +%s)
  if [ $NOW -gt $RETRY_AFTER ]; then
    kubectl label pod $POD status=queued --overwrite
    echo "Re-queued after rate limit cooldown: $POD"
  fi
done
```

When a rate-limited pod is re-queued and then released by the scheduler, the entrypoint needs to resume Claude rather than starting fresh. The entrypoint should check for a saved session ID at `/tmp/claude-session-id`. If found, use `claude --resume <id>`. Session ID capture is implemented fully in Phase 4; this ticket adds the re-queue mechanism only.
acceptance_criteria: A pod with status=rate-limited and an expired ccw/retry-after annotation gets re-queued
Re-queued pod follows normal queue flow (waits for concurrency slot)
Scheduler logs show re-queue events
Pods with future retry-after timestamps are not re-queued early

title: Add `ccw queue` CLI subcommand
description:
Implement `ccw queue` to show the current state of the queue and allow adjusting concurrency.

`ccw queue` — show queue status:
```
Queue Status
  Running:      2/2 (at limit)
  Queued:       3
  Rate-limited: 1 (retry in 2h 15m)

Queued tasks (oldest first):
  other-app-20240315-c1d2    feat/refactor    queued 45m
  third-20240315-e4f5        main             queued 32m
```

`ccw queue set-limit <n>` — update maxConcurrent in the ConfigMap:
```bash
kubectl patch configmap worker-config -n claude-workers \
  --patch "{\"data\":{\"maxConcurrent\":\"$n\"}}"
```

`ccw queue promote <task>` — immediately release a specific queued task (bypass normal ordering).
acceptance_criteria: `ccw queue` shows running/queued/rate-limited counts
`ccw queue` shows time until rate-limited pods retry
`ccw queue set-limit 3` updates maxConcurrent in the ConfigMap
`ccw queue promote <task>` immediately releases a queued pod
All output is readable and consistently formatted
